items.prompt: Black to move. What is White threatening? Name the move.

claims.statement: If Black passed, Qxf7 would be mate.
Two white pieces attack f7.
One black piece defends f7.

hints: Count the attackers of the f7 pawn, and the defenders.
The bishop and the queen both look at the same pawn.
A queen capture on f7 that ends the game.
items.explain: The queen and the bishop both attack f7, and only the king defends it. If Black does nothing, Qxf7 is checkmate (the engine confirms mate in one).

items.prompt: Black to move, facing the same threat. Meet it with a move that also helps your game.

claims.statement: g6, Qe7, Nh6 and Qf6 are all within 60 centipawns of the best move.
Nf6 loses by force (mate).
d5 is at least 100 centipawns worse than the best move.

hints: Either attack the queen or guard f7 a second time.
A pawn can attack the queen; a piece can guard f7.
g6, Qe7, Nh6 and Qf6 all deal with it.
items.explain: Each accepted move either attacks the queen or guards f7. The natural-looking Nf6 ignores the threat: Qxf7 is then checkmate. The pawn move d5 attacks the bishop but the engine rates it much lower.

feedback_by_move.g8f6: A normal developing move, but it does not stop Qxf7, which is checkmate.
feedback_by_move.d7d5: It attacks the bishop, but the engine rates it at least 100 centipawns below the accepted moves at depth 16.

items.prompt: Black to move in this old trap position. Pick a sound developing move.

claims.statement: Nc6, Qd7, Nf6 and Be7 are within 50 centipawns of the best move.
h6 is at least 100 centipawns worse than the best move.

hints: Black's bishop on g4 has a knight in front of it and the white queen behind.
Develop a piece instead of pushing a rook pawn.
A knight to c6 or f6, the queen to d7, or the bishop to e7.
items.explain: Any of these moves develops a piece. The rook-pawn move h6 looks like a pin-breaker, but it allows the knight capture on e5, and the engine rates it at least 100 centipawns lower at depth 16.

feedback_by_move.h7h6: It asks the bishop a question, but White answers with Nxe5. The engine rates h6 at least 100 centipawns below the accepted moves.

items.prompt: Black to move. White has just taken the pawn on e5, and Black's bishop could take the white queen. Find the move the engine prefers.

claims.statement: dxe5 is the engine's first choice.
Bxd1 loses by force (mate).
Even after the best reply Black is clearly worse (at least 1.5 pawns, depth 16).

hints: Before you capture the queen, ask what the capture takes away from your own king.
After Bxd1, which white piece gives check on f7, and who covers d5?
Take the knight on e5 with the pawn.
items.explain: Bxd1 wins the queen, but White answers Bxf7+ Ke7 Nd5#, a forced checkmate. The calm dxe5 is the engine's choice at depth 16; White then takes the bishop and Black is behind, but not mated.

feedback_by_move.g4d1: It wins the queen, but Bxf7+ Ke7 Nd5 is checkmate: the engine finds a forced mate.

items.prompt: Black has taken the queen with Bxd1. White to move: find the forced mate in two.

claims.statement: Bxf7+ forces mate in two.

hints: Black's king has few squares and the e5 knight watches d7 and f7.
The bishop can give check on f7. Which square must the king take?
Bxf7+ and then a knight move.
items.explain: Bxf7+ is check. The knight on e5 guards f7 and d7, so the king can only go to e7, and Nd5 is mate.

items.prompt: White to move. Black has taken back on d5 with the knight. Find White's strongest idea.

claims.statement: Nxf7 and d4 are within 60 centipawns of the best move and of each other.

hints: Black's king is still on e8 and f7 is guarded only by the king.
A piece can be given up to pull the king into the open.
The knight on g5 captures on f7. A central pawn move is also strong.
items.explain: The knight sacrifice on f7 drags the black king forward; the engine rates Nxf7 and d4 about equally at depth 16.

items.prompt: Black to move. Recapturing on d5 with the knight allows a famous attack on f7. Choose a different move.

claims.statement: Na5, Nd4 and b5 are within 70 centipawns of the best move.
Nxd5 is at least 60 centipawns worse than the best move.

hints: Which white piece is attacking f7, and which black piece would be dragged away from guarding it?
The bishop on c4 is the other attacker. Can you attack it or block it?
The knight on c6 can go to a5 or d4, or a pawn can go to b5.
items.explain: Declining the recapture avoids the f7 attack. The engine rates Nxd5 at least 60 centipawns below the best move at depth 16, and the three accepted moves are within 70.

feedback_by_move.f6d5: The natural recapture, but it allows Nxf7. The engine rates it at least 60 centipawns below the best moves at depth 16.

items.prompt: Black declined the recapture with ...Na5. White tries the same sacrifice, 6.Nxf7. Does it work? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: 6.Nxf7 is at least 250 centipawns worse than the best move.

hints: Where is the black knight that was on d5 in the earlier line?
After Kxf7, is there a check that wins time?
items.explain: With the knight on a5 instead of d5, the sacrifice just loses a piece: the engine rates 6.Nxf7 at least 250 centipawns below White's best move at depth 16.

items.prompt: White to move. Is 4.Ng5, attacking f7, a good try here? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: 4.Ng5 is at least 300 centipawns worse than the best move.
One black piece attacks g5.

hints: Who can capture on g5?
Which black piece looks along the diagonal toward g5?
items.explain: Black's queen attacks g5 along the open diagonal, so the knight is simply taken: the engine rates 4.Ng5 at least 300 centipawns below White's best move at depth 16.

items.prompt: Both sides have castled. White to move. Is the bishop sacrifice 6.Bxf7+ a good try? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Bxf7+ is at least 300 centipawns worse than the best move.
Two black pieces defend f7.

hints: Count the defenders of f7 now.
Is the king alone there?
items.explain: After castling, the king and the rook both guard f7, so the sacrifice only loses a piece: the engine rates Bxf7+ at least 300 centipawns below White's best move at depth 16.

items.prompt: White to move. Is 4.Ng5, attacking f7, a reasonable try here? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: 4.Ng5 is within 40 centipawns of the best move.
No black piece attacks g5.

hints: Who can capture on g5?
Does the knight on f6 get in the black queen's way?
items.explain: Here the knight on f6 blocks the queen's diagonal, so nothing attacks g5. The engine puts 4.Ng5 within 40 centipawns of White's best moves at depth 16. That makes it playable, not forced.
